about.title: Palmdale Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A space heater that shorts out during an Antelope Valley cold snap. A child seat that gives way when a family braking on Palmdale Boulevard is hit from behind. A power tool that kicks back in a garage off Rancho Vista Boulevard. Product defects show up in ordinary Palmdale life, and when they do, California law treats the claim differently from most injury cases. Under strict liability, you usually do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. What matters is whether the product had a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or an inadequate warning, and whether that defect caused your injury. Responsibility can extend from the factory to the distributor to the store where you bought it. Palmdale is home to roughly 158,000 people in northern Los Angeles County, and the city recorded 815 injury collisions in 2025; a portion of crash injuries anywhere trace back to airbags, tires, or brakes that did not perform as designed. LawProactive is free to use. We connect you with an independent attorney who reviews your situation and works on contingency.

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: You generally do not need to show the maker was negligent, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. An attorney in our network can help frame the claim around design, manufacturing, or warning defects.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Counts
items.desc: California allows claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers alike. That matters when the maker is overseas and the store where you bought the item is on Avenue S.

items.title: Evidence Guidance From Day One
items.desc: The product itself is often the single most important piece of evidence. We connect you quickly so an attorney can advise on preserving it before it is discarded, repaired, or returned.

items.question: My airbag never deployed in a crash on Sierra Highway. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It could be both. The driver who caused the crash may be responsible for the collision, while the vehicle or airbag manufacturer may be strictly liable if the system was defective and that failure worsened your injuries. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has looked at it. An independent attorney can sort out which claims apply.

items.question: I threw the broken product away. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Losing the product makes a case harder, but not always impossible. Photos, receipts, packaging, model numbers, recall notices, and medical records can still help establish what the item was and how it failed. Contact an attorney as soon as you can so nothing else is lost.
